documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PHYSICIAN NOTE - 02/03/2025 19:50

25-year-old woman with borderline personality disorder, depression and bulimia nervosa, previously seen here for self-inflicted cuts, brought in by her roommate, who found her sleepy and confused with an empty sertraline bottle beside her.

Home meds per pharmacy fill history: ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone daily. (Sertraline - see HPI.)
NKDA. Never smoker, no EtOH.

Vitals: HR 110, BP 130/85, RR 16.
Exam: somnolent, rouses to voice, follows simple commands. Pupils dilated, reactive. Mucous membranes dry. Tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs: Na 140, K 4.0, Cl 100, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 90. Ethanol not detected. Urine drug screen negative for common drugs of abuse. Salicylate pending at time of this note.

Impression: intentional sertraline ingestion with serotonin toxicity.
Plan: IV fluids, lorazepam IV as needed for agitation, cardiac monitoring, poison center consulted, admit to medicine. Psychiatry to see when medically appropriate.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 02/03/2025 - Discharged 02/05/2025
Service: Hospital Medicine

Principal diagnosis: Serotonin syndrome following intentional sertraline overdose.
Other: borderline personality disorder; major depressive disorder; bulimia nervosa; recurrent UTI.

Course: Admitted from the ED after ingesting a bottle of sertraline. Salicylate level returned undetectable. Managed with IV fluids, telemetry and as-needed lorazepam. Mental status cleared and heart rate settled within about 24 hours. Sertraline was held during the stay. Psychiatry consultation on 02/04: impulsive overdose in the setting of chronic emotional dysregulation, no ongoing suicidal intent, safety plan completed with the patient, outpatient follow-up appropriate. Psychiatry recommended resuming sertraline 100 mg at discharge.

Discharge medications: sertraline 100 mg daily (resume); ethinyl estradiol 0.035 mg / norethindrone 1 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; outpatient psychiatry within 2 weeks.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called within 2 business days of discharge. Pt home, roommate there. Has her discharge paperwork, restarted sertraline yesterday as instructed. Denies confusion, tremor, fever. Denies SI. Psychiatry appt 2/18. Confirmed PCP visit Monday 2/10 at 1:30.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit. Admitted 2/3-2/5 for serotonin syndrome after taking her bottle of sertraline. Discharge summary reviewed.

She remembers little of that evening. Says she was 'done with everything' after a bad week but now says she didn't really want to die. Back on sertraline 100 since discharge. No tremor, sweats, or confusion. Sleep poor. Not back at work yet, going back Thursday.

Exam: alert, tearful at times, oriented. HR normal, no clonus, reflexes normal, pupils normal. Vitals as charted.
PHQ-9 18. Asked about current SI: passive at times, no plan or intent today. She agreed to the safety plan from the hospital and we went through it line by line. Roommate is helping hold onto medications.

A/P
1. Serotonin syndrome - resolved.
2. Intentional overdose / MDD / BPD - continue sertraline 100 per psychiatry; will now send 30-day supplies only, no auto-refill. Psychiatry 2/18. Therapist this week.
3. TCM: medication reconciliation done, records reviewed.
RTC 1 month, call anytime.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Re: Sophia Labrie

Seen 02/18 and 03/20/2025 after her February admission for serotonin syndrome. She is engaged with individual therapy again and her mood is slowly improving; she denies current suicidal thinking. Diagnoses: borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder. Medication: sertraline 100 mg daily, unchanged. Return here in 2 months.

Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit, just turned 26.

Since last year: overnight ED stay June 2024 for cutting; admission Feb 2025 for sertraline overdose with serotonin syndrome. Seeing psychiatry every 1-2 months and therapy weekly. Mood 'better than February.' No self-harm since February. No purging per her. No urinary symptoms since November.
Meds: sertraline 100 mg daily (30-day fills), OCP daily. NKDA.
SH: back at work part time. No tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: thin, well groomed, weight stable. Vitals as charted. Eyes and ears normal. Thyroid nonpalpable. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no tenderness or masses. Skin with old forearm scars, nothing new. Normal gait.
PHQ-9 13. No SI.

A/P
- Preventive: Pap normal 2024, next 2027. HIV/HCV done. Flu and COVID this fall.
- Purging history: CBC, CMP today.
- MDD/BPD: continue current plan, psychiatry managing.
- OCP: BP normal, continue.
RTC in a few months.

documents.body: Sophia, your blood count and chemistry panel are normal, including potassium and kidney function. No changes.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrived 08/21/2025 16:15

Chief concern: took acetaminophen to end her life, about 2 hours prior.

26F, BPD, MDD, bulimia nervosa, prior ED visits for cutting and an admission in February for sertraline overdose. She swallowed 'a handful' of extra-strength 500 mg acetaminophen around 14:15. Roommate found the empty bottle, which held 50 tablets, and drove her in. No symptoms. She says she regrets it.

Meds on file: ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone daily. NKDA. No tobacco or alcohol.

Vitals normal. Exam: alert and oriented x3, no distress, no RUQ tenderness, otherwise unremarkable.

Labs: acetaminophen 150 mcg/mL at 16:30 (about 2 h after ingestion) - too early to plot. CBC, LFTs, INR sent. Repeat level at 4 h: 162 mcg/mL, above the treatment line. AST/ALT and INR normal.

Plan: IV N-acetylcysteine, standard 21-hour regimen, started 19:20. 1:1 sitter. Admit to medicine. Poison center aware. Psychiatry once medically clear.

documents.title: Medical Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Hospital Medicine Discharge / Transfer Summary
Admit 08/21/2025 - Transfer 08/22/2025

Diagnoses: acetaminophen toxicity, intentional (suicide attempt). Borderline personality disorder. Major depressive disorder.

Course: 4-hour acetaminophen level 162 mcg/mL. Completed the 21-hour IV N-acetylcysteine protocol without reaction. AST, ALT and INR normal on arrival and again at completion. No hepatotoxicity. Continuous observation throughout.

Medically cleared 08/22. Transferred to the inpatient psychiatric unit for suicide attempt.
Home medications (per patient): sertraline 100 mg daily; ethinyl estradiol 0.035 mg / norethindrone 1 mg daily.

Hospital Medicine

INPATIENT PSYCHIATRY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 08/22/2025. Discharge 08/29/2025.

Reason for admission: suicide attempt by acetaminophen overdose, transferred from medicine after N-acetylcysteine treatment.

History: 26-year-old woman with borderline personality disorder and major depressive disorder, chronic self-injury, a February 2025 sertraline overdose, and bulimia nervosa. Family history of maternal depression, paternal substance use and suicide of a maternal uncle.

Hospital course: participated in groups and individual sessions; developed a written crisis plan; family meeting with roommate by phone. Mood improved over the week; by discharge she denied suicidal ideation, intent or plan and was future oriented. No medication changes were made.

Discharge diagnoses: borderline personality disorder; major depressive disorder; suicide attempt.
Discharge medications: sertraline 100 mg daily; ethinyl estradiol 0.035 mg / norethindrone 1 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry 09/04; therapist 09/02; PCP within 1 week. Medications to be held by roommate.

Inpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Acetaminophen overdose 8/21, NAC, LFTs never rose; then a week on the inpatient psych unit, home 8/29. Both summaries reviewed today.

She was quiet but talked more as the visit went on. Says this was the first time she 'actually meant it.' Now: no SI, no intent, no plan; names her roommate and therapist as supports, saw therapist yesterday, psychiatry tomorrow. Roommate keeping her meds and there's no acetaminophen in the apartment now.
No RUQ pain, no nausea, no jaundice.

Exam: no scleral icterus, abdomen soft and nontender, liver edge not felt. Vitals as charted.
PHQ-9 15.

A/P
1. Acetaminophen toxicity - treated, no liver injury in hospital; hepatic panel today to close the loop. Resolved.
2. Suicide attempt, MDD, BPD - sertraline 100 continues, 30 days at a time. Crisis plan from the unit in her chart. I'll check in by phone in 2 weeks.
3. Med rec done.

documents.body: Called as promised. She's back at work three mornings a week. Saw psychiatry 9/4, no changes. No SI. Sleeping better. She asked if she can do her flu shot in October - yes, nurse visit. Next PCP visit December.

ED Record
02/18/2026 21:30

Friends brought her in after finding her at home confused and agitated. They say she has been down lately and think she may have overdosed on 'her medication.' Known to us: BPD, prior ED visits for self-harm and overdose (sertraline 02/2025, acetaminophen 08/2025).

Home meds (records): sertraline 100 mg daily; ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone daily. NKDA.

Arrival: HR 120, BP 90/60.
Exam: confused, agitated, tachycardic. Pupils dilated. Skin dry. Brief generalized seizures, on and off, in the department.

Labs: Na 140, K 4.0, HCO3 22, Cr 1.0. Blood pH 7.31. Urine drug screen positive for tricyclic antidepressants.
ECG: QRS 120 ms with occasional PVCs.

Assessment: tricyclic antidepressant overdose with seizures, QRS widening and hypotension.
Treatment: IV lorazepam for seizures, IV sodium bicarbonate in boluses then infusion, IV fluids. Poison center consulted. Admit ICU.
Source of the tricyclic not established.

documents.title: ICU and Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Critical Care / Medicine Discharge Summary
02/18/2026 - 02/21/2026

Principal diagnosis: tricyclic antidepressant overdose, intentional, with seizures, QRS prolongation and hypotension.

ICU course (02/18-02/20): bicarbonate boluses followed by infusion. QRS 98 ms on the morning ECG of 02/19 and stayed narrow. No seizures after the ED. Blood pressure recovered with fluids alone. Mental status normal by 02/20. Moved to the medical floor 02/20.
Floor (02/20-02/21): stable. Psychiatry consulted; recommended inpatient psychiatric admission.

No tricyclic was on her medication list, and where the tablets came from was not determined.

Transfer medications: sertraline 100 mg daily (held in ICU, restarted 02/21 per psychiatry); ethinyl estradiol 0.035 mg / norethindrone 1 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Transferred to inpatient psychiatry 02/21/2026.

documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
MEDICAL ICU - DISCHARGE / TRANSFER SUMMARY
Admission 06/08/2026, transfer to psychiatry 06/11/2026

Presentation: 27-year-old woman with borderline personality disorder and several prior overdoses, among them a tricyclic overdose about four months ago, brought in by friends who found her unresponsive at home next to an empty bottle labeled amitriptyline.

Home medications (records): sertraline 100 mg daily; ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone daily. NKDA.

On arrival: T 39.1 C, BP 85/50, HR 120, RR 22. Drowsy, rouses to voice. Pupils dilated. Bowel sounds diminished. ECG with QRS 120 ms.

Course: sodium bicarbonate boluses then infusion; 2 L IV crystalloid; external cooling. BP 108/66 after fluids and QRS 104 ms on repeat ECG that morning. Afebrile by 06/09. No seizures. Bicarbonate weaned 06/10. Mentation back to baseline 06/10. Psychiatry consulted.

Diagnosis: tricyclic antidepressant (amitriptyline) overdose, intentional. Where the amitriptyline came from was not established.
Transfer medications: sertraline 100 mg daily (resumed 06/11 per psychiatry); ethinyl estradiol 0.035 mg / norethindrone 1 mg daily.
Transferred to inpatient psychiatry 06/11/2026.

Medical ICU
